blocks.x: As someone who often tastes whiskey before ever having a sip of coffee or a bite of breakfast, Allen Katz, the owner and distiller of New York Distilling, has strong opinions about what makes the best whiskey glass. And it’s not just about aromatics. “There’s an emotional context,” Katz says.
Our top picks

The glass Katz reaches for during those early morning whiskey evaluations is a “juice glass.” It’s a small, straight-sided glass that holds five or six ounces. “I can picture Humphrey Bogart pouring a whiskey in Casablanca. I can picture Cary Grant and Eva Marie Saint in North by Northwest having a whiskey. In both cases, it’s not a fancy glass, it’s a juice glass,” he says.

Of course, that emotional, romantic connection is not the only thing Katz considers when choosing a glass. He believes the best whiskey glass is the one that best “arouses” your senses. Not in the sexual sense of the word. Calm down. He means that a whiskey glass should prepare you for the pleasure of drinking whiskey. As Katz puts it, “My brain is aroused saying, ‘I’m ready, let’s enjoy this.’”

Unfortunately, I can’t divine your favorite old TCM flick so I can’t help you find the best whiskey glass that channels those vibes. Instead, I tested 16 different whiskey glasses, judging them on how each one “aroused” my senses—and, of course, on how they delivered whiskey to my mouth. Here are the best whiskey glasses to buy.
(Editor’s note: While Katz’s favorite whiskey glass is a juice glass, I only evaluated glasses specifically designed for whiskey for this piece.)
AccordionItemContainerButton
Best rocks glass: Riedel Rocks Glass
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6aa3737bd3348d0b0a06a0b9/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/Riedel%2520Rocks%2520Glass.png

What we loved: Katz uses these glasses in his new Brooklyn bar, Jaywalker. And it’s easy to see why. The look is timeless; they have a clean, midcentury-modern appeal. The sides are deeply etched with straight lines, which continue along the underside of the glass, giving you something to run your fingers along no matter how you are holding it. The mouth is wide, so you can fit an ice cube (even a big cube) into it if you’d like. And each glass holds 10 ounces, so they can be used for cocktails as well as straight pours of whiskey.

Unlike Riedel wine glasses, these glasses are sturdy and hefty. And here’s a fun fact Katz told me: The tips of the pyramids etched into the base of the glass mark exactly two ounces. So you can freehand the perfect pour of whiskey. Plus, the glass makes the whiskey look incredible. The light shines through the spirit, refracting and sparkling, casting amber shadows on the table. Forget stained glass. Just get some Riedel whiskey glasses and a bottle of rye.

What we’d leave: The lip of the glass is not sharp by any means, but it’s not as rounded and inviting as some of the others. The wide mouth is great for easy sipping, but it does not funnel the aroma of the whiskey in the same way a Glencairn might. If you’re really looking for nuance in your whiskey, you might want to opt for a glass specifically designed for the job.
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6aaab5ffde95d30fa05138b8/master/w_1600%2Cc_limit/Riedel%2520Whiskey%2520Glass.jpg
Justine Sterling
Best budget rocks glass: Cocktail Kingdom Yarai Rocks Glass
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6aa373ced54e57063c1e34e3/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/Cocktail%2520Kingdom%2520Yarai%2520Rocks%2520Glass.png

What we loved: Talk about tactile satisfaction. These vintage-inspired glasses from Cocktail Kingdom are etched with a large diamond pattern, giving you gentle angles to fondle. The glass has just enough heft so that you feel like you’re drinking out of a substantial, sturdy vessel, but not so much that it’s actually heavy. The lip and the bottom edge are both rounded, so it’s comfortable to hold and sip from. And the glass’ somewhat squat stature means the aroma of the whiskey instantly hits you when you lift the glass. Plus, these glasses are shockingly affordable at just $7 per glass (or $61 for 12).

What we’d leave: While these glasses are the perfect size for my hands, those with large hands might feel like they’re a touch too tiny. And, though their size makes them ideal for a two-ounce pour of whiskey, either neat or on a rock, they’re too small for most cocktails. That said, they’re the exact size of glass I’ve been looking for to serve low-volume cocktails like Sazeracs or old-fashioneds.
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6aaab64b902e3b91fe42bec0/master/w_1600%2Cc_limit/Yarai%2520Whiskey%2520Glass.jpg
Justine Sterling
Best whiskey tasting glass: Glencairn
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6aa3724b9c3884355e620ef3/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/Glencairn%2520Whiskey%2520Glass.png

What we loved: Ever been to a whiskey tasting? You’ve used a Glencairn glass. It is the gold standard for whiskey tasting glasses. The glass is small, but it still has some weight to it thanks to the sturdy, solid base. It feels very comfortable to hold and fits right into the palm of your hand, so the whiskey warms and evolves over time. The unique shape helps deliver the aroma of the whiskey directly to your nostrils—you don’t have to jam your face into the glass.

What we’d leave: This is indeed the best glass for whiskey tasting—but that’s about it. You aren’t going to drink a cocktail out of a Glencairn. You’re not going to sip on some bourbon on the rocks from a Glencairn. It has a singular use. But if you’re a whiskey purist who really wants to savor the concentrated aromas of a whiskey and think it blasphemous to even consider adding ice, then this is a great whiskey glass for you.
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6aaab5fff258f9c57d7fdf47/master/w_1600%2Cc_limit/Glencairn%2520Whiskey%2520Glass.jpg
Justine Sterling
Best fancy whiskey glass: Chamvin Edo Kiriko Glass with Crumple Pattern
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6aaab380d2aa31ed030bb163/3:4/w_748%2Cc_limit/Chamvin%2520Edo%2520Kiriko%2520Whiskey%2520Glass.jpg
Chamvin Edo Kiriko Whiskey Glass with Crumple Pattern

What we loved: This crinkly glass is a real pleasure to hold. It’s light, but it doesn’t feel like you’re going to crush it in your hands. And the textures are unique and organic. It’s tall and slightly narrow, so your nose really gets in there when you lift it to your mouth to drink. It guides the aroma. The size and height make it appropriate for both a neat pour of whiskey or even a whiskey sour. If you’re looking for a unique glass that doesn’t look like any of your friends’ whiskey glasses, this is the best whiskey glass for you.

What we’d leave: It has a very specific look that won’t fit in everyone’s bar setup. And, while I personally love the look and feel, my husband did note that the texture looks a bit like plastic that melted in the dishwasher. Also, as these are handmade glasses, they are not cheap. Each glass will run you around $85 (though there are sales).
https://assets.bonappetit.com/photos/6aaab5ff38af1fe93f447a43/master/w_1600%2Cc_limit/Chamvin%2520Whiskey%2520Glass.jpg
Justine Sterling
How I tested whiskey glasses

I drank whiskey out of them. Duh. But that’s not all I did. To start, I held each glass in one hand, feeling the texture, grip, and weight. Then, I poured an ounce of the same whiskey into each glass (Basil Hayden Dark Rye, to be specific). I smelled the whiskey in order to judge how the glasses helped or hurt the aromatics. And then I took a sip, noting how the lip of the glass felt on my lips and how the whiskey poured into my mouth.
What I looked for in the best whiskey glasses
AccordionItemContainerButton
Yes, this is somewhat subjective, but part of the appeal of drinking whiskey is the visual aesthetic. And if you’re going to invest any serious money in a whiskey glass, it better be gorgeous.
AccordionItemContainerButton

As Katz says, whiskey drinking is a full sensory experience and that includes the sense of touch. “We all have fetishes,” he says. “One is a glass in hand.” I looked for glasses that gave my fingers something to explore and felt comfortable to hold.
Is it comfortable to sip from?
AccordionItemContainerButton

Katz describes the ideal whiskey glass as feeling “intimate” on your mouth. The part of the glass that touches your lip should be smooth and comfortable. No harsh, rough edges to distract from the flavor of the whiskey.
AccordionItemContainerButton
A few of the glasses I tested were somewhat difficult to drink out of without dribbling a bit. And dribbling whiskey is not only embarrassing, it’s a waste of good booze.
Does it deliver the aroma of the whiskey?
AccordionItemContainerButton

A big part of the whiskey experience is the aroma. “It’s meant to release stress, bring my shoulders and chest down in a means of saying to my brain, ‘it’s okay to start enjoying this,’ before the liquid even touches my lips,” Katz says. So I looked for glasses that amplified the scent.
How to get the most from your whiskey glass

One good way to wreck your whiskey experience, according to Katz, is improper washing. Oftentimes, your home dishwasher leaves residual film on the glass. That will make your whiskey taste off—it also probably won’t look great. “I find that, particularly the dishwasher pods that people use leave more aromatic residue than liquid detergent,” he says. Opt for a liquid detergent and make sure the glass is thoroughly dried or wash the glasses by hand to ensure the best whiskey drinking experience.
Other whiskey glasses I liked
Liiton Whiskey Glass Grand Canyon
